items.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: Peter Gabriel was also a tremendous artist and a very creative thinker.

ctx.x: A little bit. Yeah that is it. If we could qualify it and make it a stage actress as opposed to film. Because things can change. I mean it’s never absolutely pat in the same way, otherwise why go to a concert, you’d better listen to the record. But to work out a show and know what’s going to happen, just work out the strongest way of putting the music across. That’s more important for a pop artist I think than a jazz artist. A jazz artist

everybody knows is going to be different every time so it’s okay. I think somebody like Annie, where the fans really want to hear the song the way they just heard it on the record. Some of them would like it if it strays a little bit, a lot wouldn’t. Peter Gabriel was also a tremendous artist and a very creative thinker. I always respected him for going out on live tours, big tours supporting major albums, and he would just go with his band. And they would kind of do the same arrangements but they didn’t sound…
With all the things you do, if you could take a year off — not really off — and do the thing you like the best, can you nail that down? What do you really like to do the best?
